title.en: Uncertainty intervals with explicit statistical meaning

summary: Expose uncertainty type and units without treating every translucent band as a confidence interval.
objective: Show an estimate with an uncertainty band whose legend states whether it is a confidence interval, expanded measurement uncertainty or observed min-max range.
intent_signals: Show an estimate with an uncertainty band whose legend states whether it is a confidence interval, expanded measurement uncertainty or observed min-max range.
example_prompts: Show an estimate with an uncertainty band whose legend states whether it is a confidence interval, expanded measurement uncertainty or observed min-max range.

principles: Keep the estimated quantity and the meaning of its interval explicit. An observed min-max range describes the displayed observations; do not relabel it as inferential confidence.
Separate missing uncertainty from zero uncertainty. Treat selection emphasis and uncertainty styling as different channels so picking an object does not imply increased confidence.
implementation: Require interval metadata alongside bounds: target quantity, unit, interval type, method, source/revision and applicable confidence level or coverage factor. Render unknown fields as unknown rather than supplying a default 95 percent.

For measurement expanded uncertainty show the supplied U and k with the estimate; attach assumptions supporting a confidence interpretation. For mean confidence intervals show the estimator and level; for observed ranges identify the observation set.

Choose error bars for sparse point estimates, ribbons for ordered scalar samples or a separately explained spatial envelope for positional bounds. Do not turn a scalar value interval into geometric thickness without defining the mapping.

Provide numeric bounds and a legend in addition to opacity. Keep missing/censored intervals distinct and disclose any clipping; toggling uncertainty must not alter the estimate or domain scale silently.
observable_checks: Supply identical numeric bounds with different interval types: each legend and detail panel preserves the distinct meanings instead of displaying a generic confidence label.
Feed one missing interval, one zero-width interval and one asymmetric interval. All remain distinguishable, with the supplied bounds preserved.
Set U=0.2 units and k=2 without distribution assumptions: show those values without automatically claiming 95 percent confidence.

known_limits: The pattern consumes uncertainty metadata; it does not estimate uncertainty or certify calibration. Pointwise intervals do not by themselves establish simultaneous coverage of a whole surface.
Draft authored guidance; no renderer, interaction artifact or scientific result was executed for this record.
creative_affordances: Choose layout and visual emphasis to support the stated inspection task; these are design proposals rather than proven usability improvements.

claims.statement: NIST defines expanded uncertainty U as k times combined standard uncertainty; interpreting k=2 as approximately 95 percent requires the stated normal-distribution and reliable-standard-deviation conditions.
claims.scope: Measurement expanded uncertainty under the source assumptions, not a universal interval rule.

claims.statement: NIST describes mean confidence limits as uncertainty in an estimated mean and associates frequentist coverage with repeated applications of the interval procedure, not a probability assigned to a particular fixed interval.
claims.scope: Frequentist confidence intervals for a mean; no inference for arbitrary distributions or Bayesian intervals.
